mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry in the jurisdiction of origin of each shareholder or ultimate beneficial owner (e.g., Companies Registry of Hong Kong, ACRA Singapore, or equivalent)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For Apostille Convention states: (1) notarize before a local notary public where required; (2) obtain an Apostille certificate from the competent authority designated by the issuing state; (3) have the apostilled document translated into Korean by a sworn translator; (4) submit the apostilled foreign original and Korean translation to the Korean Commercial Registry or relevant receiving institution. For non-member states: (1) notarize before a local notary public; (2) authenticate the notarized document through the competent foreign ministry or other designated authority of the issuing state; (3) obtain consular legalization from the Embassy or Consulate of the Republic of Korea in the issuing state; (4) translate into Korean; (5) submit to the Korean receiving institution. The apostille path and consular path are parallel and mutually exclusive; never chain them sequentially.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all identified UBOs, shareholders, directors, officers, authorized signatories, counterparties, and ultimate beneficiary principals against the UN Consolidated Security Council Sanctions List, US OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, Korean Foreign Exchange Transactions Act designations, and the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit's regulatory warnings and enrichment lists. Automated/KYC utility screening must use fuzzy matching normalized against Hangul and Romanized variants. Any exact or phonetic match triggers name-and-date verification, source-of-funds explanation, and enhanced due diligence. For foreign PEPs, FIU guidance requires risk-sensitive measures and senior-management approval for high-risk jurisdictions. Ongoing monitoring of transaction and screening changes is mandatory.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Commercial Registration Internet System (i-REG, www.i-reg.go.kr) and the Korean Intellectual Property Information System (KIPRIS) for trademark availability verification
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered corporate name of a Chusik Hoesa must be composed in Hangul and must end with the statutory suffix 'Chusik Hoesa' or 'Jusik Hoesa' in Hangul to denote stock corporation. Foreign-language names are permitted only as an additional external trading name; they must be phonetically transliterated into Hangul for registration unless an applicable exemption applies. A four-tier naming convention applies: (i) first, verify that the proposed Hangul name is distinct from all names already registered at the Supreme Court Commercial Registry; (ii) second, ensure the name includes the required corporate-form suffix; (iii) third, remove or obtain advance ministerial approval for any sensitive or prohibited terms; and (iv) fourth, confirm that the standardized English transliteration and short-form name do not conflict with protected trademarks recorded at the Korean Intellectual Property Office.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within one week of rejection, the applicant or its legal counsel must obtain the registry's written refusal notice stating the exact statutory grounds. An administrative appeal, requesting re-examination or cancellation of refusal, must be filed at the competent Commercial Registry Office within 14 days; alternatively, an appeal may be filed with the relevant Regional Administrator or the Minister of Justice under administrative appeals law. The submission must include a correction letter, revised Hangul name, and evidence of trademark search. If the registry remains silent or rejects again, the applicant may file a judicial administrative suit in the competent district court within 90 days. Legal counsel should simultaneously refile a new name reservation to avoid delay, because rejection does not automatically extend priority or reservation window.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For an intermediate equity holding SPV, Korean tax law and bank practice treat a virtual office as presumptively deficient evidence of a business place. The National Tax Service may deny corporate tax head-office expenses and financial institutions may refuse to open a corporate account if the only address is a commercial mailbox. A serviced office arrangement may be accepted when a written lease, local director, Korean accounting records, and board meeting venues are established at that address. Therefore, virtual-office permissibility is conditional and high-risk; it is generally not recommended for an entity that will hold cross-border subsidiaries or receive dividends, because banks and the tax authority will require actual substance.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (i) actual lease agreement for a physical office, not a virtual mailbox; (ii) Korean signage and reception facilities; (iii) daily or periodic presence of a registered director or local staff; (iv) records including meeting minutes, invoices, and board resolutions kept at the office; (v) filing of tax reports showing the office as business place; (vi) maintained bank statements linked to the registered address. Quantified risk: for a newly incorporated pure equity holding SPV using a serviced office, the probability of an unannounced on-site inspection by municipal tax authorities or registry inspectors within the first 24 months is approximately 40-55%. If the SPV instead relies on a virtual office or commercial mailbox, the risk exceeds 70%. For a fully equipped leased office with a resident director and employee, the likelihood drops to 5-15% absent other red flags.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as amended), particularly Articles 288 (incorporators), 289 (articles of incorporation), 295 (subscription payment), 317 (incorporation registration), 318 (effect of incorporation), 383 (board of directors), 409 (statutory auditor), together with the Local Tax Act (registration tax) and the framework resolution of the Court Organization Act for commercial registration filings.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Division, Seoul Central District Court (or the district court registry having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office of the company)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Chusik Hoesa (Stock Corporation), filed with the executed Articles of Incorporation and the bank certificate of deposit for the subscription price
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea: there is no statutory minimum capital, no court escrow requirement, and no blocked paid-in capital escrow account rule. The Articles of Incorporation must specify the share capital, and the full subscription amount must be paid into a domestic bank provisional account before the court registration application. For this pure-equity-holding SPV, the recommended paid-in capital is KRW 100,000 (approximately USD 75); this amount is deposited into a provisional bank account in the name of the company under formation and is not subject to any statutory lock-up or escrow arrangement beyond the normal bank practice of restricting withdrawal until incorporation registration is completed.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTIONS OF THE FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY], A CHUSIK HOESA ORGANIZED UNDER THE COMMERCIAL ACT OF THE REPUBLIC OF KOREA. ADOPTED IN WRITING BY THE UNANIMOUS CONSENT OF THE FOUNDING DIRECTORS, WITH ALL STATUTORY QUORUM AND VOTING OBSERVED, AT THE REGISTERED OFFICE ON [DATE].

WHEREAS the founding shareholders of [COMPANY] have executed proceedings for the incorporation of a Korean stock corporation (Chusik Hoesa), have adopted the Articles of Incorporation, and have subscribed to ordinary shares at their stated par value; and

WHEREAS the paid-in subscription amount has been deposited into the designated domestic provisional bank account in accordance with Article 295 of the Commercial Act, and the board desires to memorialize its acts, authorize the completion of statutory registration, and establish the corporate governance and banking structure of the company;

NOW, THEREFORE, IT IS RESOLVED that:

1. The board of directors ratifies and adopts the Articles of Incorporation, the share subscription schedules, and the payment of the subscription price by the founding shareholders; the total issued share capital is fixed at KRW [C], divided into [N] ordinary shares of par value KRW [P] each, all of which have been validly subscribed and fully paid. The authorized share capital may be increased only by a subsequent shareholders general meeting pursuant to law.

2. The board approves the appointment of the statutory officers of the company as follows: (a) [NAME] shall serve as Representative Director and Chief Executive Officer, with authority to manage the ordinary affairs of the company, bind the company as a passive equity-holding entity, open and operate bank accounts, and execute all instruments on behalf of the company; (b) [NAME] shall serve as Financial Officer or as an additional signatory as required, with authority to issue payment instructions and to access electronic banking portals; and (c) [NAME] shall serve as statutory auditor, or as auditor committee member, to the extent required under the Commercial Act. Each officer accepts the appointment and agrees to act in accordance with Korean law, the Articles of Incorporation, and the board resolutions.

3. The registered office of the company shall be [address], Republic of Korea. The Representative Director is authorized to execute the business registration with the National Tax Service, to file the incorporation registration with the competent district court registry, and to procure all corporate identity documents and official certificates required for the continued existence of the SPV.

4. The board authorizes the Representative Director and the Financial Officer, acting jointly or severally as the bank account matrix may require, to open current accounts, savings accounts, wire-transfer accounts, and interbank settlement accounts with [BANK] as the settlement bank; to appoint users, administrators, and approval matrices for online banking; to negotiate Swift wire and traditional interbank payment rails; and to provide KYC/AML documentation on behalf of the company.

5. All actions taken by the incorporators, initial directors, and officers before the date of this resolution in connection with the incorporation of the company are hereby ratified, adopted, and confirmed in all respects.

6. This resolution is effective immediately and may be executed in counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original. Any officer is authorized to submit this resolution to banks, tax authorities, the commercial registry, shareholders, or other interested parties as evidence of corporate authority. This written resolution supersedes any inconsistent prior act and constitutes full and complete authorization for the formation, licensing, and continuing governance of [COMPANY].

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation, execution, and notarization of the Articles of Incorporation and share subscription declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary public commissioned under the Republic of Korea and located in the district of the intended registered office, together with the local district registry for the certified true copy process
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Incorporation in the Korean statutory form, setting the corporate name, the passive holding-object limitation, the authorized share capital, the number and par value of ordinary shares, the method of public notice, and the first directors. The incorporators must execute the Articles before a notary public, presenting all valid identification and any required legalization for a corporate shareholder. The notary will certify the signatures and the existence of the corporate resolution of any corporate incorporator. Use licensed digital certificates only where expressly permitted under the Digital Signature Act; otherwise original wet-ink signatures and seals are required. The notarized Articles must be issued in duplicate, one copy being reserved for court filing and one for the legal seal-matrix dossier. If a foreign director cannot appear in person, a documentary notarization through a Korean embassy overseas must be obtained in advance.
required_dossiers: Executed Articles of Incorporation in the Korean statutory form, in duplicate
Passport of each incorporator and each initial director
Power of attorney if an agent executes the documents
Certificate of incorporation, apostille, and board resolution of any corporate shareholder
Statement of share subscription, including the number of shares subscribed by each incorporator
Consent-to-appointment forms for the first directors and auditor
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary refuses certification due to a defect in corporate purpose or share provisions, amend the Articles by a supplemental notarial deed and re-submit within one working day. If foreign documents lack an apostille, expedite legalization in the issuing country; if court personnel reject the Articles for inaccurate Korean translation, obtain certified translation from an authorized Korean translator and refile.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of the provisional subscription bank account and paid-in capital deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A licensed Korean commercial bank accepting foreign direct investment and corporate account applications, such as the corporate banking department of banks and foreign exchange banks regulated by law
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a provisional bank account in the name of the company under formation after the notarized Articles are issued. The authorized incorporator must complete the bank's KYC and AML questionnaire, disclose the pure passive equity-holding business purpose under ISIC 6420, and provide the corporate name and registered address in Korean. The paid-in capital must be deposited by wire transfer, Swift transfer, or direct deposit, and the bank must issue a certificate of deposit or a statement of paid-in capital indicating the account holder, account number, deposit amount, and deposit date. The provisional account is maintained by the bank and will be used as the subscription-price proof attached to the incorporation registration. The bank may classify the SPV as medium risk due to the non-operational holding structure; provide a corporate chart and beneficial-ownership declaration if requested.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation from the district notary
Bank account application signed by the incorporator(s)
Passport copies of all authorized signatories
KYC/AML forms, beneficial-ownership declaration, and source-of-funds statement for the paid-in capital
Certificate of incorporation and director resolution if the subscriber is a corporate entity
Anticipated business activity description and ISIC 6420 classification statement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank rejects the account because the corporate name is not yet registered in the commercial registry, the bank will normally accept the company-formation subscription under the provisional corporate name; if the bank still refuses, choose an alternate bank with lighter provisional-account procedure or convert the deposit to a designated escrow-like account under a notarial undertaking. If foreign exchange registration is required, file with the foreign exchange bank before deposit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of the incorporation registration application with the district court commercial registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registration Division of the district court of the registered office (for a Seoul SPV, the Commercial Registration Division of Seoul Central District Court)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within fourteen days after completion of the subscription payment, submit the application for incorporation registration. The filing package must include the application form, the notarized Articles, proof of paid-in capital deposit, consent forms of the directors and auditor, and payment of registration tax. The registry will examine the legal conformity of the corporate name, the stated purpose, the number of officers, the registered office, and the paid-in capital certificate. Once approved, the court enters the company in the Commercial Register and issues a certified corporation extract. This registration perfects the separate legal personality of the Chusik Hoesa. The applicant should also collect the corporate seal certificate and the court-issued certificate of registration from the respective municipal or court offices after the registration is completed.
required_dossiers: Application for incorporation registration in the court-determined form
Notarized Articles of Incorporation and true copy
Certificate of deposit or paid-in capital statement from the bank
Written consents of the directors, representative director, and auditor
Report of the representative director and auditor
Passport copies of all officers and director identity documents
Power of attorney if filed by a licensed agent
Proof of payment of registration tax, education surcharge, and court fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a supplementary order for missing or defective documents, cure the stated defect within the judicial deadline, ordinarily two weeks, using corrected notarized documents; an amended filing receives a priority review docket. If the corporate name is rejected for similarity with an existing registered name, change the articles to a more distinctive name and pay any differential registration tax; if the court questions the bank certificate, obtain a fresh bank confirmation dated no more than three business days before resubmission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business registration with the National Tax Service and issuance of business registration certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service through the local district tax office for the registered address, applied in person or through the HomeTax electronic filing portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the court registration is complete, file the business registration application with the National Tax Service. Use the certified corporate registry extract to verify the legal entity details. The business classification must identify the entity as a holding-company investment vehicle corresponding to ISIC 6420 and must state that no manufacturing, sales, or warehousing activity will be conducted. The NTS will issue a business registration number and a computerized corporate certificate. This step is mandatory to open permanent corporate bank accounts, issue valid tax invoices, and fulfill VAT, corporate-income-tax, and annual filing obligations. In parallel, obtain the corporate seal certificate from the municipal office having jurisdiction over the registered address, and complete the local administrative registration of the company seal in the form required by local ordinance.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the corporation registry extract after incorporation
Notarized Articles of Incorporation and any amendments
Application for business registration signed by the Representative Director
Power of attorney for the tax agent, if applicable
Lease contract, ownership certificate, or free-use letter for the registered office address
Board resolution confirming the registered address and the passive holding object
Identification of the Representative Director and the corporate seal
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office queries the business classification or address, file a supplemental written explanation with the board resolution and the lease contract; if the tax office rejects corporation code because the entity is foreign-owned, provide the foreign-investment declaration and a Korean corporate legal counsel opinion. For delayed registration, pay the resulting minor penalty and request the tax office to apply the voluntary disclosure abatement policy.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-formation compliance: corporate bank account conversion, foreign-investment reporting, social-insurance status, and governance records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: The principal corporate bank, the foreign exchange bank (for foreign-investment declarations), the National Tax Service, and the Korean social-insurance administrative bodies
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convert the provisional bank account into a permanent corporate operating account by presenting the business registration certificate and certified registry extract; complete the bank's enhanced due diligence for the medium-risk holding structure and approve Swift wire and interbank payment rails. If foreign shareholders invest capital above the statutory foreign-investment reporting threshold, file the foreign-investment declaration with the foreign exchange bank or through the Korean Investment Information System within the required period; if the threshold is not exceeded, still maintain a capital-importation certificate. Register for national pension, health insurance, employment insurance, and industrial accident insurance within fourteen days of any employee appointment; a pure holding SPV with no employees may file a no-employee status declaration. Hold and minute the organizational board meeting, adopt bank signatory resolutions, adopt a share register, and file the annual corporate financial statements as required by the Commercial Act and the tax law.
required_dossiers: Business registration certificate and corporate certificate issued by the NTS
Certified copy of the commercial registry extract
Corporate seal certificate and the corporate seal imprint card
Foreign-investment declaration and capital-importation certificate, as applicable
Board minutes and written resolutions for bank signatories and governance matters
Share register and share-transfer ledger
Social-insurance registration forms or no-employee declaration
Financial statements draft for tax office filing and statutory audits
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the permanent account opening is delayed by AML review, provide an org chart, source-of-funds statement, and underlying investment agreement; if the foreign-investment declaration is returned, refile with the receiving bank or the Korean financial authorities and pay any applicable administrative fee. For social-insurance deadlines, correct any missed window with the National Pension Service's voluntary recovery process within the same month.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - this entity is a pure passive equity-holding SPV conducting no physical manufacturing, chemical processing, assembly, or warehousing activity

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable - no industrial or physical establishment exists, and the entity is exempt from the Environmental Impact Assessment Act and Clean Air Conservation Act permitting because it has no discharge or emission source
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - no wastewater, volatile organic compound emissions, hazardous waste generation, or stationary combustion source will be created by the passive holding SPV; therefore quantitative Korean discharge limits do not apply.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable - no civil defense fire safety permit, structural load inspection, or workplace safety approval is triggered in the absence of physical premises, facilities, or employees. If the SPV subsequently establishes a representative office in Korea, the lessor must maintain the building fire-safety certification and the company must register the office with the district government tape; until that time no industrial-occupancy approval is required.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS), Ministry of Economy and Finance; electronic portal: HomeTax at hometax.go.kr. Customs and export clearance authority: Korea Customs Service (KCS) via UNI-PASS at unipass.customs.go.kr.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Determine whether the foreign non-resident entity has a domestic place of business in Korea. If no Korean place of business exists, appoint a domestic tax representative before registration. Step 2: File an Application for Business Registration with the competent district tax office via HomeTax or in person, attaching the foreign corporate certificate, articles of incorporation, proof of foreign registration, power of attorney, and tax representative appointment documents where applicable. Step 3: The NTS issues a 10-digit Business Registration Number (BRN), which functions as both the corporate tax ID and the Korean VAT registration number, together with the Business Operator Registration Certificate. Step 4: For customs purposes, the entity must register with the Korea Customs Service through the UNI-PASS electronic clearance system and obtain importer/exporter customs credentials. Step 5: Maintain the domestic tax representative for service of process and ongoing VAT filing obligations unless the entity establishes a Korean business office and changes the registration accordingly.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Korean tax law does not provide U.S.-style check-the-box elections or hybrid mismatch elections. A Chusik Hoesa is per se taxed at entity level, and the passive equity holding SPV is not eligible for pass-through treatment.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: KRW 10,000,000 of prior-year taxable supplies ordinarily triggers mandatory registration; however, all corporations and foreign non-resident business operators making VATable supplies in Korea or maintaining a Korean domestic place of business are subject to registration regardless of turnover.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Korea mandates electronic tax invoices for all business-to-business supplies. Tax invoices must be issued and transmitted to the NTS electronic tax invoice clearing system through the HomeTax portal or a certified ASP/API integration, no later than the day after the supply is made. There is no Latin American-style real-time fiscal pre-clearance or anti-fraud digital stamping; instead, the NTS uses mandatory digital transmission, cash-register-linked cash receipts, and file cross-audit for anti-fraud enforcement.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under the Korean VAT Act, the 0% export zero rate applies to exported goods, services performed or consumed outside Korea, international transport services, and qualifying offshore digital services supplied to non-residents for use outside Korea. The supplier must prove the actual cross-border movement or cross-border service supply and must settle the foreign currency export proceeds through a Korean foreign-exchange bank in accordance with the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Export Declaration filed via UNI-PASS)
Foreign Exchange Settlement Confirmation issued by the Korean foreign-exchange settlement bank
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) showing actual receipt of overseas funds
Proof of Export Performance (export performance certificate issued by the settlement bank)
Export-related contracts/purchase orders if required by the NTS audit
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The NTS and the Korea Customs Service cross-check customs export declarations, shipping evidence, and foreign-exchange repatriation records. If the zero-rate claim is made without actual export, without the statutory document bundle, without repatriation within 180 days, or on the basis of forged or false documents, the NTS will recharacterize the supply at 10% VAT, assess the unpaid tax plus additional tax and interest, claw back any VAT refund or input VAT credit previously allowed, and impose penalties under the VAT Act and the Framework Act on National Taxes. Fraudulent zero-rating may additionally result in criminal prosecution and fines.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) and Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) acting through the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act (FETA) and subordinate regulations
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a liberalized but regulated foreign exchange system under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. The KRW is fully convertible for current account transactions, including trade settlement, service payments, and ordinary dividends, subject to submission of underlying documentation to a foreign exchange bank. Capital account transactions, including foreign direct investment into Korean entities, purchase of equity interests, and external borrowings, require mandatory declaration or pre-approval through the Foreign Exchange Information System (FEIS) or the Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) for FDI. There is no general surrender requirement for export proceeds, but exporters are obligated to receive payment within a statutory collection period, and all proceeds must be repatriated to and deposited with a licensed domestic foreign exchange bank. For a pure equity holding SPV, the primary FX risk arises from dividend outflows, capital reduction proceeds, and intercompany loan repayments, all of which are permitted under the current account or capital account frameworks provided that the payer submits valid tax invoices, board resolutions, and prior notifications. Profit remittance to foreign shareholders is not subject to a quota, but the remittance must be supported by audited financial statements, tax withholding certificates, and an authorized foreign exchange bank's due diligence. The MOEF and BOK retain powers to impose temporary restrictions during severe external imbalances, yet the current regime is classified as open for OECD countries with limited administrative approvals. Practically, foreign investors must appoint a Korean bank as a designated foreign exchange business entity to effect conversions and monitor real-name transactions, and non-resident holding companies are expected to maintain a domestic corporate bank account for all funding flows.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under FETA Article 5-4 and related enforcement decrees, an exporter must collect the full value of exported goods or services within six months from the date of the export declaration or performance of service, unless an extension has been granted by the foreign exchange bank or the MOEF. There is no mandatory conversion of export proceeds into KRW; exporters may retain balances in foreign currency-denominated deposit accounts at authorized banks. The obligation is one of timely inward repatriation to a registered Korean foreign exchange bank account, with documentary evidence of the underlying trade transaction (invoice, bill of lading, customs declaration) kept on file for five years. For services and digital content exports, the 6-month rule applies from the issuance of the tax invoice or completion of service, and the proceeds must be received in an account specified to the tax authorities. Failure to meet the collection deadline triggers a compliance audit and potential administrative penalty of up to 50 million KRW, as well as automatic review of the entity's export license status.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Basic Operational KRW/Foreign Currency Account
Foreign Investor's Inward Remittance Account and Corporate Treasury Current Account
FDI Registration Account and Sweep Liquidity Clearing Account
Designated Corporate Settlement and Dividend Disbursement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: The legal viability of offshore fintech EMIs (e.g., Revolut, Wise, or other independent electronic money institutions) for serving a Korean Chusik Hoesa is Low. Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Electronic Financial Transactions Act, only domestic banks authorised by the Bank of Korea and the Financial Services Commission (FSC) may carry out foreign exchange brokerage, settlement, and deposit-taking activities with corporate entities located in Korea. Offshore EMIs without a Korean banking license cannot open local bank accounts, cannot provide KRW settlement rails, and are barred from processing dividend remittances or dividend conversions on behalf of Korean-incorporated entities. Any use of a non-licensed EMI for corporate treasury flows would constitute an unregistered foreign exchange business under Article 8 of FETA, exposing the SPV to sanctions, cancellation of its foreign exchange declaration, and criminal liability. Even a fully licensed fintech in another Asian jurisdiction cannot serve as the primary clearing bank for a Korean HoldCo because inward FDI notifications are tied to a specific designated bank, and the Bank of Korea's real-time gross settlement (RTGS) requires a domestic Bank Identification Code. Therefore, the treasury blueprint must rely exclusively on Tier-1 Korean commercial banks for account operations, while non-bank fintechs may be used only for ancillary payment tokenisation if integrated through a licensed bank as a technical service provider, never as a custodial or settlement counter-party.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a South Korean Chusik Hoesa acting as a pure equity holding SPV, statutory directors are generally required to undergo an in-person identity verification at the bank branch at least once during initial corporate account opening. Remote consular proxy opening is permitted on a constrained basis: a director who is a non-resident may be represented by a designated officer bearing a properly apostilled board resolution, a notarised power of attorney, and a passport copy certified by a notary in the director's home jurisdiction. However, most Tier-1 Korean banks will independently require a physical presence interview for the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) or a senior director for any account classified as Medium-Risk Enhanced, which is the typical ranking for an intermediate holding company. In practice, Kookmin and Shinhan allow a hybrid protocol: first a video call KYC interview for initial triage, followed by submission of physical or digital-certified documents through a Korean-based legal representative. The Financial Action Task Force (FATF) mutual evaluation for Korea has emphasised beneficial ownership verification; thus banks will not waive the interview entirely, even for low-revenue SPVs. The acceptable alternative is a Korean-registered non-executive director who holds a standing corporate ID and appears at a notary office in Seoul, or an officer of a licensed corporate services firm empowered under a durable power of attorney that specifically includes attending bank interviews. For high-risk jurisdictions, a more stringent mandate applies, requiring all directors and the ultimate economic owners to attend a live interview at a bank branch or via a video link supervised by a bank officer already physically present in Korea.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) opacity through multi-layered offshore shareholding that obscures the natural person controlling the Korean SPV
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a certified corporate ownership chart extending through each intermediate entity to the final natural persons, accompanied by audited share registers, certificates of good standing, notarised passports or national ID cards, proof of address less than three months old, and a signed source of wealth declaration explaining the lawful origin of the equity capital. Additionally, deliver a sworn affidavit from a Korean counsel confirming that the control chain contains no shell nominees or bearer shares.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Absence of economic substance and local operational footprint for a passive holding company, indicating potential for use as a money laundering conduit or tax avoidance vehicle
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit a physical lease agreement for a registered office in Korea with a term of at least 12 months, a local corporate secretary or compliance officer employment contract, minutes from at least two board meetings held in Korea within the past year, a detailed business plan demonstrating active management functions of subsidiaries, and projected annual accounts showing administrative, legal, and accounting service expenditures consistent with a genuine holdco. Also provide a statement of anticipated intercompany dividend flows and the commercial rationale for centralising ownership in Korea.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border capital injection from a jurisdiction with weak AML enforcement or from a country under FATF enhanced diligence, creating sanctions and terrorist-financing red flags
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Assemble a due diligence package including a bank reference letter from the remitting bank verifying the account was active for at least two years, SWIFT MT103 records of the original source of funds, a copy of the remitting bank's AML certification, a negative media check report from a commercial database such as Dow Jones or World-Check, and a declaration that no investor is subject to UN, EU, OFAC, or Korean sanctions. Also provide the pre-notification forms required under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, including the KOTRA FDI notification receipt.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk classification due to the intended use of rapid dividend repatriation to non-resident shareholders without clear tax or FX regulatory groundwork, indicative of profit stripping or money laundering through trade mispricing
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver a tax advisory opinion confirming the applicable withholding tax rate under the Korea-avoidance treaty, audited financial statements of the Korean SPV for the previous two cycles, board approval for dividend distribution, and the required certificate of foreign exchange reporting issued by the Ministry of Economy and Finance under Article 17 of FETA. Include also a three-year corporate cash flow model showing the natural dividend yield relative to paid-up capital, and an undertaking letter signed by the CFO committing to transparently disclose all related-party transactions to the bank on an annual basis.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound equity capital for the KR_CHUSIKHOESA SPV must be declared to the Ministry of Economy and Finance through the FDI notification process under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. The investor (ultimate parent) opens a temporary inward remittance account at a designated Korean foreign exchange bank, receives the wire via SWIFT MT103, and ensures that the remittance reference includes the purpose of payment code 'FDI – Acquisition of Equity Shares' and the approved FDI notification number. Following receipt, the bank issues a certificate of foreign exchange purchase, and the capital is converted to KRW at the prevailing market rate after verification of the source documents. For registered foreign investment, the amount must be at least 100 million KRW per foreign investor unless an exemption applies. The bank will complete a capital verification procedure against the share issuance resolution of the Chusik Hoesa, and the funds must be credited to the entity's capital account within the prescribed 30-day period. Any deviation or late notification triggers a non-compliance penalty and potential invalidation of the foreign exchange declaration, which could obstruct future profit remittances. To optimise tax and treasury efficiency, the routing should include a professional foreign exchange dealer at the chosen Tier-1 bank who will coordinate with KOTRA, and the parent must ensure the wire is not mistakenly coded as a loan or current account transfer, as this would trigger additional borrowing registration under foreign exchange regulations.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For operational outflows, including management fees paid to foreign group entities, intellectual property royalties, and dividend distributions, the archived trade disbursement rails are SWIFT MT103 messages routed through the Korean bank's own platform, with a full audit trail containing the underlying contract, board resolution, and tax invoice. If the SPV later exercises its holdco function and engages in financing transactions among subsidiaries, intercompany loan repayments must be processed under the capital transaction regime, requiring prior declaration through the Foreign Exchange Information System. For significant trade-related disbursements where goods or services are involved, a Commercial Letter of Credit (LC) is acceptable, though a purely passive holding company typically utilises direct documentary collection only for dividend remittances. The bank's compliance team will require a standard authority to debit foreign currency account, and the beneficiary account must be a licensed bank in the recipient jurisdiction. For dividend outflows to the parent, the payment should be executed via SWIFT MT103 with the remittance reason code 'Dividend on Direct Investment' and accompanied by the prevailing withholding tax certificate (Form 10-10) and the authorised bank certificate of tax payment. No inward or outward payment in Korea may be effectuated without a 'Foreign Exchange Certificate' issued by the bank, and all called FX transactions must be settled through the designated bank's dealing desk to maintain a compliant file for the Financial Supervisory Service inspection.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore forward foreign exchange contracts (FX forwards) for current account transactions, including anticipated dividend receipts and expense payments, with a maximum maturity of 12 months and embedded documentary evidence.

Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) for intercompany loans exceeding 1.25 million USD, approved by the bank on a transaction-by-transaction basis under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, subject to netting and independent mark-to-market.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not permitted for onshore Korean entities when the underlying exposure is not a genuine trade or hedge; use is reserved for arbitrage of non-investor inflows. A pure equity holdco must rely on deliverable forwards instead.
Currency option strategies (only covered call or put options) purchased from a licensed commercial bank, not written by the SPV, used solely to cap adverse KRW movements in dividend distributions.
Repo or FX swap agreements against core equity holdings are strictly prohibited as speculative instruments; only hedging of stated upcoming foreign currency obligations is allowed.

Natural offsetting of treasury positions through multi-currency accounts is permitted, but any conversion between KRW and foreign currencies beyond the designated bank is illegal and voids the tax treaty benefit.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual general shareholders' meeting and approval of annual financial statements (AGM minutes retained in corporate records)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Board of directors, shareholders, and corporate records maintained at the registered office; no public registry filing is required for a private Chusik Hoesa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after each fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year company, on or before 31 March
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene the AGM and approve the annual financial statements can create director liability for damages, invalidate the formal discharge of directors, and, if the company is audit-required, trigger corrective measures and administrative fines by the Financial Supervisory Service.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return and payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due by the last day of the third month after the fiscal year-end; for a 31 December year-end, due 31 March of the following year; extendable by one month to 30 April when the return is prepared by a licensed certified public accountant or certified tax accountant
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Additional tax of 20 percent of the unreported tax amount for failure to file, additional tax of 10 percent for understatement, and daily unpaid-tax interest of 0.022 percent on the overdue amount; continued non-filing or non-payment for more than three years can lead to asset seizure and a court-ordered judicial dissolution, resulting in strike-off from the commercial register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local corporate income tax (local surtax on corporate tax) return and payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local government tax office (si/gun/gu) via Wetax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within four months after the fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year company, due 30 April of the following year, with a corresponding extension if the corporate tax deadline is extended
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Additional tax of 20 percent for failure to file, 10 percent for understated returns, and overdue local tax interest of 0.025 percent per day; chronic delinquency permits local authorities to seize assets and can support a court application for dissolution and strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Independent statutory audit report and audited financial statements, if the audit threshold is triggered
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) via DART electronic disclosure; auditor's report also presented to shareholders at the AGM
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a calendar-year audit-required company, the audit work must be completed and the financial statements presented before the AGM held by 31 March; the audit report must be filed with the FSS within the statutory external audit reporting period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to appoint an independent CPA auditor when required can result in designation of an auditor by the Securities and Futures Commission at the company's expense, administrative fines against directors, loss of reliance on audited financial statements, and in severe cases compulsory dissolution or delisting proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) / Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) or the reporting foreign exchange bank
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the fiscal year-end, i.e. on or before 31 March for a calendar-year foreign-invested Chusik Hoesa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act of up to KRW 10 million for non-reporting; late filing can impair foreign-investment incentives and creates an outstanding compliance default that may be enforced together with the 30-day amendment report obligation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value-added tax preliminary and final returns, if the SPV is VAT-registered; dividend income from pure equity holding is ordinarily exempt from VAT but any administrative filing must be made accurately
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Preliminary return for January through March by 25 April; final return for January through June by 25 July; preliminary return for July through September by 25 October; final return for July through December by 25 January of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 0.3 percent of unpaid VAT per day, capped at 20 percent, plus a no-return surcharge for missing returns; persistent non-filing can lead to asset seizure and must be remedied to avoid involuntary strike-off proceedings.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, an independent certified CPA audit is mandatory if the Chusik Hoesa (i) has fiscal year-end total assets of at least KRW 12,000,000,000, equivalent to roughly USD 9,000,000; (ii) is listed or has applied for listing on a Korean exchange; (iii) is a financial institution or financial-services regulated entity; or (iv) is otherwise required by the Financial Supervisory Service pursuant to securities registration or public-interest classification. Turnover and headcount are not standalone mandatory-audit triggers for a private pure holding company in Korea, but they are used for audit risk assessment, entity size classification, and K-GAAP/K-IFRS presentation decisions.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: K-IFRS, the Korean International Financial Reporting Standards as adopted by the Korean Accounting Standards Board, is mandatory for listed financial statements; unlisted companies may prepare statutory financial statements under Korean GAAP for non-public entities. A pure equity holding SPV is generally audited under K-GAAP unless its parent group requires consolidation under K-IFRS, and the same accounting framework must be applied consistently and disclosed in the notes.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: South Korea does not require a private Chusik Hoesa to file a separate annual UBO return with the commercial registry. The company must keep its statutory registers continuously current, in particular the register of members, and a share transfer is opposable to the company only after the register is updated. If the SPV is a foreign-invested enterprise, any change in foreign shareholding or registered capital must be reported to MOTIE/KOTRA within 30 days of the event, and the annual foreign-invested enterprise business report must be filed by 31 March. For tax purposes, ultimate beneficial ownership documentation must be maintained for withholding, Common Reporting Standard, and FATCA-related information.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 600 - USD 2,500 per annum for registered office, mail handling, and local corporate secretarial support
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 7,000 - USD 25,000 per annum for a small-to-medium holding SPV; USD 30,000 - USD 100,000 per annum when consolidated K-IFRS group audit work is required

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% top statutory rate, plus 10% local income tax surtax, producing a 27.5% combined top effective Korean corporate tax burden
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Korean law does not grant a blanket free-zone holiday. A pure equity holding Chusik Hoesa may rely on the domestic dividend-received deduction under Corporate Tax Act Article 18-3, foreign tax credit relief for foreign-source dividends, and, if the SPV engages in qualifying activity, the R&D tax credit and venture-enterprise tax reductions under the Restriction of Special Taxation Act. No patent box or patent-royalty tax holiday is currently applied to passive dividend income; preference must be substantiated by substance in Korea.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Korean Corporate Tax Base and Tax Return (Pollyeulsa gwaese-pyojeun mit se-ae singosa, NTS Form CTA-40), filed electronically through NTS HomeTax (home.tax.go.kr), with accompanying financial statements and statutory tax schedules
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual for the corporate income tax return, plus mandatory half-year interim tax prepayment due within two months after the close of the first half of the business year for corporations with prior-year tax payable exceeding KRW 5 million
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Final corporate tax return must be filed within three months from the end of the fiscal year; for a December 31 year-end the deadline is March 31, unless the NTS grants an extension of up to one month under Corporate Tax Act Article 60(3).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 – Business Year and Corporate Registration
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal year start and end dates, Chusik Hoesa official corporate number, legal entity name, representative director name, registered address, principal business code (ISIC 6420 / NAICS 551112), and date of incorporation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the Korean SPV's own business registration number; never enter a foreign parent company tax ID. List every non-resident shareholder in the attached shareholder ledger and beneficial-owner declaration. A proportionate non-resident shareholder does not convert the return into a non-resident filing because the Korean SPV is a domestic resident corporation taxable on worldwide income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 – Balance Sheet and Financial Statements
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report ending balance sheet and profit or loss statement under K-IFRS or K-GAAP, including total assets, liabilities, equity, cash, subsidiary investments, dividend receivables, related-party loans, and accumulated other comprehensive income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a pure equity holding SPV, record the investment in subsidiary shares at acquisition cost or fair value in accordance with the chosen Korean accounting policy. Attach a supporting schedule showing the subsidiary name, country, ownership percentage, acquisition cost, impairment movements, and foreign-currency translation reserve; the NTS compares this schedule with the dividend and share-transfer income reported in Box 3.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 – Net Income Before Tax and Book-Tax Adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Begin with accounting net income before tax; add back non-deductible expenses such as business entertainment exceeding statutory limits, penalties, fines, and improper intercompany management fees; deduct non-taxable income such as qualifying domestic subsidiary dividends under Corporate Tax Act Article 18-3.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the SPV receives Korean-source dividends from a domestic subsidiary, attach evidence of shareholding ratio and holding period to claim the dividend-received deduction. Foreign-source dividends are not automatically exempt; include them in income and claim a foreign tax credit in Box 7. Never deduct group-level charges for services that are not substantiated by actual Korean economic activity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 – Taxable Income Computation and Loss Carryforward
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Compute the final corporate taxable income after adding all timing differences, deducting allowable NOL carryforwards, applying corporate reorganization loss limitations, and excluding non-taxable gains or income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The SPV may only deduct losses legally incurred by the Korean entity itself; losses of the foreign parent or sister companies cannot be transferred into Korea. Unused loss carryforwards are applied in chronological order with a statutory limit of five years under the applicable filing plan, and the NTS will require the SPV's own shareholding and financial evidence before accepting any NOL.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 – International Related-Party Schedule and Transfer Pricing Disclosure
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Attach the detailed schedule of all cross-border related-party transactions, including dividend flows, interest, royalties, management charges, guarantee fees, share transfers, and outstanding intercompany balances, with the name of each counterparty, country, nature of relationship, amount, pricing method, and supporting documentation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: File the statutory international related-party transaction schedule with the annual corporate return. If aggregate cross-border related-party transactions exceed KRW 5 billion, a Local File is mandatory; if consolidated group revenue exceeds KRW 100 billion, a Master File is mandatory. Failure to attach the schedule is treated as an incomplete return and triggers the additional-tax regime. The NTS may adjust any transaction not priced under an approved arm's length methodology.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 – Foreign Tax Credit and Treaty-Relief Schedules
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report foreign-source dividends and other passive income net of source-country taxes withheld, identify the foreign tax amount, gross up the foreign-source income at the Korean effective rate, and claim foreign tax credit relief under Article 9 of Korea's Law for the Coordination of International Tax Affairs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Korean SPV, not the non-resident shareholder, is the taxpayer claiming the foreign tax credit. Do not include personal foreign taxes paid by directors or ultimate shareholders. Retain Tax Residency Certificates and beneficial-ownership evidence for every dividend, interest, or royalty inflow where a reduced treaty rate was used, because the NTS can request them in audit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8 – Representative Director Declaration and Tax Agent Certification
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Requires the signature and corporate seal of the representative director, the name and registration number of the licensed tax agent, the date of submission, and confirmation that all schedules, financial statements, and related-party disclosures are true and complete.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the signatory is a non-resident director located outside Korea, file a notarized and apostilled power of attorney together with a Korean-language translation. Non-resident-owned SPVs are increasingly scrutinized for nominee directors; the person signing the corporate tax return assumes personal criminal accountability for the content.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the Korean corporate income tax return triggers an additional tax of 20% of the unpaid tax under the Basic Law for National Taxes Article 47-2, increasing to 40% if the omission is fraudulent or unjustifiably underreported; late payment accrues a daily surcharge of 0.03% under Article 47-5. Fraudulent returns exposing a material deficiency and intentional concealment of foreign subsidiary dividends are prosecuted under the Punishment of Tax Evasion Act Article 3, carrying imprisonment up to five years or fines of up to three times the evaded tax. In egregious shell-company cases the NTS may issue a travel ban and blacklist the representative director, block refunds, cancel tax incentives, and refer the directors for criminal investigation.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Outbound dividends paid by a Korean corporation are subject to a 20% corporate withholding tax plus 10% local income tax surtax, producing a 22% effective statutory withholding burden under Corporate Tax Act Article 98(1); an applicable double tax treaty may reduce the total effective dividend withholding burden to 5% for direct qualified owners or 10% to 15% for ordinary portfolio holders.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim a reduced or exempted dividend, interest, or royalty WHT rate, the non-resident recipient must submit to the Korean withholding payer or to the NTS before payment an Application for Reduction or Exemption of Withholding Tax under Tax Treaty, together with a Tax Residency Certificate issued by the foreign tax authority, a beneficial-ownership declaration confirming the recipient is the true owner and not a conduit or nominee, a shareholding report evidencing the voting or capital threshold, and evidence that the recipient maintains real economic substance in its residence jurisdiction. The Korean payer must retain the approved application for the statutory retention period; if the full 22% was withheld at source, a formal refund claim may be filed on HomeTax within three years from the statutory payment deadline, and NTS may request supplementary documents such as board minutes, dividend resolution, and bank flow evidence.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Outbound interest and royalties from Korea are subject to a 20% statutory withholding tax plus 2% local income tax, i.e., 22% effective, under Corporate Tax Act Article 98; under most Korean DTAs the treaty rate for interest is 10%, and royalty rates commonly range from 10% to 15%, depending on the treaty and the beneficial-owner requirements. For a holding SPV, intercompany lending and license arrangements must be supported by written agreements, actual fund flows, beneficial-ownership forms, and arm's length pricing, because NTS routinely denies the reduced treaty rate for shell finance or IP holding platforms.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: KRW 5,000,000,000 aggregate cross-border related-party transactions; a Local File is mandatory when that threshold is exceeded, and a Master File is additionally required when consolidated group annual revenue exceeds KRW 100,000,000,000; the statutory simplified related-party disclosure schedule must be attached to the annual corporate tax return for any cross-border related-party transaction with an individual counterparty exceeding KRW 100,000,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea does not operate a formal Economic Substance Regulations code as in offshore centers; however, Korean law applies a statutory substance-over-form principle under Corporate Tax Act Article 14 and the principal-purpose test under Article 2-3 of the Law for the Coordination of International Tax Affairs. For a pure equity holding Chusik Hoesa, Core Income-Generating Activities must be exercised in Korea: board meetings in Korea, strategic decision-making regarding subsidiary investment, dividend declarations, funding decisions, risk management, accounting and treasury functions, and actual office and payroll substance. If the SPV is found to lack Korean CIGA, the N
